subject: MSA/Order Form - proposed uptime bands, credit tiers & maintenance windows
messages:
From: Sally Chen <sally.chen@paloma.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@paloma.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines and order form — uptime and credits

Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the paperwork. Attached are Paloma's redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (Paloma_redline_MSA_v3.pdf, OrderForm_Paloma_v2.xlsx). High-level asks from our side: 

- Uptime targets: we proposed 99.9% for production services and 99.5% for non-production.
- Credits: we expect a per-incident sliding credit tied to affected customer traffic (sample formula included in the spreadsheet). We also asked for a hard cap of 100% of monthly fees per calendar month.
- Response times: P1 = 1 hour, P2 = 4 hours, P3 = 24 hours.
- Maintenance windows: we proposed a weekly 02:00–04:00 UTC window for routine jobs or, alternatively, a monthly 4–6 hour maintenance window with 48 hours notice.

A couple of items worth flagging up-front: we need visibility into planned maintenance (portal or email notices), and we want an explicit fallback for capacity failures (e.g., automated regional failover or documented runbook).

Can we schedule a 30–40 minute sync earlier next week to walk through the redlines and identify non-starters (legal/product)? Our procurement team wants to close by end of June if possible.

Thanks,

Sally Chen
Head of Procurement, Paloma Systems
Sally Chen | sally.chen@paloma.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Paloma_redline_MSA_v3.pdf (redline), OrderForm_Paloma_v2.xlsx (order form)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@paloma.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines and order form — uptime and credits

Sally — thanks for sending these over and for the target cadence. I read the redlines and pulled the most material items for product/legal review below. Happy to take a call; I can do Monday 10–11am PT or Tuesday 1–2pm PT — let me know what works.

Quick notes from an ops/product perspective:
- Uptime: Redwood's standard for production customers is 99.95% monthly. For non-prod we typically guarantee 99.5% (agree with your separation). Would you accept 99.95% for prod and 99.5% for non-prod as a compromise?
- Credits: we prefer a monthly credit cap equal to the monthly invoice amount (not cumulative across multiple months). Your proposed per-incident sliding scale is reasonable; we ask for a clause that limits credits to a single crediting event per incident window to prevent overlapping credits.
- Response SLAs: Redwood can commit to P1=1 hour response/acknowledgement, but mitigation/resolution ETAs vary by root cause. We prefer to call these "response/acknowledgement" SLAs rather than full resolution SLAs.
- Maintenance: Product prefers consolidating routine maintenance into a monthly 4-hour window with up to 72-hour notice. Weekly windows introduce more churn for live customers. We can support scheduled weekly tasks if they are low-impact and documented, but won't treat those as "maintenance-free" time.

Operational asks from my side for Paloma:
1) Can you share a sample traffic mix or peak qps so we can validate capacity planning?
2) Are there region-specific restrictions (e.g., EU-only data) we should be aware of?
3) Please confirm procurement timeline.

I'll loop in Lauren and Jonas to capture legal / commercial redlines in writing after their review. If we get alignment on the three bullets above we can translate into clean MSA language.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Head of Account Management, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0137
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: Paloma MSA redlines — legal position summary

Team — quick internal summary after reviewing Paloma_redline_MSA_v3.pdf. High-level positions and suggested alternative language below. We should be deliberate about what we concede versus what product must own.

1) Uptime measurement and credit calculation
- Paloma's redline ties uptime to "customer-reported" availability and a per-customer traffic weight. We should insist on Redwood's telemetry as the authoritative measurement (we publish per-region availability metrics to the Console).
- Proposed compromise language: "Availability will be measured using Redwood's published metrics for the relevant service region; credits will be calculated per-month using the standard credit matrix, not on a per-customer weighting."

2) Credit cap and accrual
- We can accept a sliding scale of credits. We will push for a combined cap: credit <= monthly invoice for the impacted service in any single calendar month; credits do not roll forward.
- Avoid language that allows cumulative credits to exceed the customer's monthly recurring fee over multiple months without a material breach threshold.

3) Response vs. Resolution
- Do not agree to resolution-time guarantees (too dependent on third-party infra). Offer response/acknowledgement commitments and reasonable best-effort resolution targets with incident classification and communication SLAs.

4) Maintenance windows
- Counterproposal: scheduled maintenance up to 6 hours/month with 72 hours notice; emergency maintenance allowed with post-event notification and no credits if emergency maintenance was required to remediate a security issue or critical remediation.

5) Evidence and runbooks
- Paloma asked for a documented failover/runbook. We can provide an operations runbook summary and monthly scheduled maintenance calendar, but we should not publish internal runbooks or sensitive architecture diagrams in the MSA. Provide an "Operations Annex" that references an internal runbook for escalation (redacted).

Next steps: Jonas, can you review the exact wording for the availability measurement clause (sample below) and return suggested edits by Monday AM? I'll draft a short addendum covering maintenance carveouts and credit cap language so we can present a clean compromise.

Sample availability clause (for discussion):
"Availability for each Service is measured using Redwood's region-specific telemetry as reported in the Redwood Console. For the purposes of this SLA, Availability is calculated monthly as: (Total minutes in month - total minutes of unavailability) / Total minutes in month. Service Credits, if any, will be applied per the standard credit matrix and capped at the invoiced amount for the impacted Service for that calendar month."

-Lauren

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA redlines and order form — uptime and credits

Sally/Tom — thanks for your patience while we reviewed the redlines internally. Below is a proposed compromise we can take to your legal/procurement team; if that looks reasonable we can circulate a redlined MSA (attached) and a revised Order Form.

Proposed compromise (summary):
- Uptime: 99.95% monthly for Production Services; 99.5% monthly for Non-Production Services.
- Credits: Sliding credit matrix (as discussed) with a cap equal to the monthly invoice for the impacted Service in any single calendar month. Credits do not roll forward. Credits are applied one time per incident window; overlapping incidents will be handled per Redwood's incident adjudication policy.
- Response SLAs: P1 = acknowledgement within 1 hour; P2 = acknowledgement within 4 hours; P3 = acknowledgement within 24 hours. Resolution targets will be provided as mitigation ETAs in the incident communication but are not legally guaranteed.
- Maintenance windows: Scheduled maintenance up to 6 hours per calendar month with 72 hours advance notice. Emergency maintenance (security or critical remediation) may be executed with post-event notice; such emergency maintenance does not trigger Service Credits.
- Measurement: Availability measured using Redwood's region-specific telemetry, published to the Console. If either party disputes the measurement, the parties will engage in a technical review and the Console telemetry will be the primary source of truth.

Operational notes / asks we need from Paloma before we finalize:
1) Estimated peak/95th percentile QPS and samples of workload (simple spreadsheet).
2) Any region-specific data residency requirements (e.g., EU-only).
3) Confirmation you can accept the credit cap as described above.

If you confirm in principle we will share a redlined MSA with the draft availability clause and an updated Order Form. We can also propose a 30-day pilot period under these terms for the first customer cohort to validate metrics before a long-term commit.
